questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to declare an abstract class in C#?
questions.explanation: The 'abstract' keyword marks a class as abstract, meaning it cannot be instantiated directly and may contain abstract members.

questions.prompt: Which keyword is used to declare an abstract method inside an abstract class?
questions.explanation: Abstract methods must be declared with the 'abstract' keyword and have no implementation body.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to declare an abstract class named Vehicle.
Can an abstract class be instantiated directly?
options: Only if it has no abstract methods
questions.explanation: Abstract classes cannot be instantiated. You must create a concrete subclass and instantiate that instead.

questions.prompt: Arrange the correct order for declaring an abstract class with an abstract method and an overriding implementation.
Which access modifier is required for a method to override an abstract method in a derived class?
questions.explanation: The 'override' keyword is used in the derived class to provide an implementation for an inherited abstract method.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank to mark a method as abstract.
Which statement about abstract classes is TRUE?
options: They can contain both abstract and non-abstract methods
questions.explanation: Abstract classes may contain fully implemented (non-abstract) methods alongside abstract ones, and they can have constructors called by derived classes.

questions.prompt: Write a simple abstract class Shape with an abstract method Area() and a concrete class Circle that overrides it.
When should you use an abstract class?
options: When you want multiple inheritance of behavior
When you want to share common code among related classes
When you need value type semantics
When you want to define only method signatures
questions.explanation: Abstract classes are ideal when you have a base class relationship with shared implementation, while interfaces are better for defining contracts across unrelated types.
